title: The Long Game
teaser: Indigo dye pits, a decade of ledgers, and four million dollars a year that vanished into Switzerland.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kano. The old city walls glow red in the morning, and the dye pits of Kofar Mata breathe indigo into the air.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hadiza Lawan had her father's ledgers open on her knees when the letter came.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.text: Hadiza. You always saw what I missed. Count the money. Someone has been counting it for me. — G.O.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: Count the money. You never asked me for anything, Chief. And now you're gone.

choices.text: Open every ledger tonight. All ten years.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: Bring me tea. A great deal of tea.

choices.text: Call Kolade in Lagos. Bankers know where money hides.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Hadiza Lawan, calling me? I'm flattered. And suspicious.

choices.text: Tell no one. Not even family.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: In Kano, the walls listen. Then they talk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Midnight at Kurmi market, among the lanterns and bolts of bright cloth, she finds it.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: Four million dollars a year. Every year. Out of Confluence Holdings and into a private bank in Geneva.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: Banque Moreau. Someone has been bleeding the Chief for a decade, and nobody noticed.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Moreau? Very old, very private, very Swiss. Why do you ask?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He answers a little too smoothly.

scenes.prompt: This is either evidence or leverage.

choices.text: Send it to the other heirs. Nobody wins a rigged game.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: Let them all see. Thieves hate the light.

choices.text: Keep it. Whoever holds this holds the crown.

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: My father taught me: never show your best cloth on the first day of the market.

choices.text: Send it to one person only: the 'N.D.' in the margins.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: In the margin of the oldest ledger, in the Chief's handwriting: 'For N.D., if anything happens to me.'

response.speaker: hadiza
response.text: Nabyen Dalyop. Jos. Let's see who you are.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sallah Durbar. Horsemen in red and gold, trumpets, dust, the whole city cheering.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And in the middle of it all, a man in a Lagos suit, sweating.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Hadiza. I came all the way to Kano to make you an offer.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: You have the numbers. I have the bank. Together we walk into Port Harcourt already wearing the crown.

scenes.prompt: Kolade Balogun, House of the Lagoon.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Then I'll see you on the other side of the table.

choices.text: Ask him about Banque Moreau. Watch his eyes.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: He blinks. Once. Then he laughs.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Hadiza has played enough cards to know a bluff.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Before she leaves, a boy brings a calabash of kunu, 'with the Lagos gentleman's compliments.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Hadiza tips it onto the sand. The sand hisses and turns black.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: Someone wants me to think Kolade did this. Which means someone is very afraid of what I've found.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Evening. The last flight south out of Mallam Aminu Kano International.

lines.speaker: hadiza
lines.text: Port Harcourt. Let's see who's lying.

outcomes.title: Open Books
outcomes.text: Hadiza showed everyone the truth. Honest, brave, and now a target.

outcomes.title: The Blade
outcomes.text: Hadiza kept the proof to herself. In a game of thrones, the one who knows the most usually wins. Usually.

outcomes.title: For N.D.
outcomes.text: Hadiza found a name in the Chief's margins and followed it. N.D. Nabyen Dalyop. Why did a billionaire write a gem trader into his ledgers?

reflections.text: Kolade's laugh came a second too late.
Lagos and Kano have shaken hands. For now.

s_greed.title: Circled three times
s_greed.text: GREED, circled three times in red ink in the margin of the 2019 ledger, in the Chief's own hand. He knew, a year before he died.

m_kano.title: Indigo Morning
m_kano.text: Red walls, indigo pits, and a letter that said: count the money.

m_durbar.title: The Durbar
m_durbar.text: Horsemen in red and gold, and a Lagos banker in the dust.

k_ledger_page.title: A torn ledger page
k_ledger_page.text: Four million, out. Four million, out. Four million, out. Every line initialled E.M.
